expected_symptom: f(1) against overloads f(unsigned int)/f(int) reports 'call to f is ambiguous' naming both candidates; f(1u) compiles cleanly
history: always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (linear scan, 20 stable releases, 0 invalid probes) plus main-debug
reviewed_by: gpt-5.3-codex (independent batch-019 step-10 review; applied selectively at collation)
summary: Confirmed on main (89e2f98e2) and on all 20 probeable stable releases v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607: f(1) is rejected as ambiguous between f(unsigned int) and f(int), while f(1u) compiles cleanly, matching the issue exactly. Maintainer (llvm-beanz) already confirmed same-day this is DXC's broken overload resolution, to be fixed by the planned HLSL 202x C++-overload-rules adoption. New finding: the successor Clang-based HLSL front end (hlsl_clang_trunk on Compiler Explorer) already compiles the identical source with no diagnostic, while still correctly rejecting a genuinely-ambiguous control (f(1.0f)) with identical wording to classic dxc -- so the fix is real and already realized there, just not in classic dxc.exe.
title: signed/unsigned overload resolution error seems unjustified
